name: Grade 7 IIT: Scratch Programming Foundations
description: Scratch sequences, sprites, events, variables, selection, comparisons, logic operators, loops, debugging, and pair programming.

words.definition: A block-based programming tool used to make games and animations.
words.example: The class built a quiz in Scratch.

words.definition: A character or object in a Scratch project.
words.example: The sprite moved when the key was pressed.

words.definition: A group of connected blocks that run together.
words.example: The script made the sprite speak and move.
A green flag event started the sequence.
The sequence changed costume before playing sound.

words.definition: A named place that stores a value that can change.
words.example: The score variable changed during the game.

words.definition: The information stored in a variable.
Code that chooses what happens based on a condition.
words.example: Selection gave different responses for right and wrong answers.

words.definition: A rule that can be true or false.
words.example: The condition checked whether the answer was correct.

words.definition: A symbol or word used to compare or combine values.

words.example: The comparison tested if score was greater than 5.

words.definition: Rules used to make decisions in programs.
words.example: AND, OR, and NOT are logic operators.
The repeat loop replaced copied blocks.
Iteration made the animation shorter to code.

words.definition: To find and fix a coding problem.
words.example: The student debugged the condition block.

words.definition: To follow code step by step to understand what happens.
words.example: Tracing helped find the wrong variable value.

words.definition: The pair-programming role that controls the keyboard or mouse.
words.example: The driver built the blocks while the navigator checked logic.

words.definition: The pair-programming role that checks, guides, and suggests.
words.example: The navigator spotted a missing loop.
